findings.text: Single buffer descriptor keeps CPU pointer in buf alongside device address in dma alongside extent in len, forming the common unit exchanged with the DMA engine in either direction.

Receive DMA bundle carries polling controls poll_rate plus poll_timeout plus auto_poll_rate alongside timer support in timer, alongside progress markers running plus cookie, alongside descriptor pair dbuf_b plus dbuf_a chosen by use_buf_b, alongside linkage complete plus chan, alongside bookkeeping last_jiffies plus last_residue.
Transmit DMA bundle holds queued marker alongside buf pointer alongside len extent alongside dma address alongside chan handle, tracking one outstanding device mapping at a time.

Port wrapper extends generic serial state in port with translation table in reg_offset and vendor profile in vendor and clock handle in clk, interrupt bookkeeping old_status plus im, sizing fixed_baud plus fifosize, short name store type, console completion flag console_line_ended, RS485 timing rs485_tx_drain_interval with state rs485_tx_state and timers trigger_stop_tx plus trigger_start_tx, and optional DMA image dmacr with usage flags using_rx_dma plus using_tx_dma and engines dmatx plus dmarx and probe marker dma_probed.

RS485 transmit sequencer admits idle OFF plus active SEND plus pre-transmit WAIT_AFTER_RTS plus post-transmit WAIT_AFTER_SEND plus delayed post-transmit WAIT_AFTER_SEND_DELAY, with moves driven by start and stop requests and drain and delay timers converging back to idle.

ST register translation keeps standard positions for data with flags with baud with control with interrupt with DMA controls while diverting timeout with watermark and split line formats and flow plus autobaud plus integration-test extensions to ST-specific positions, including ABIMSC with ABCR with ITIP with ITCR with XOFF2 with XOFF1 with XON2 with XON1 with XFCR with TIMEOUT with DMAWM, with receive and transmit line halves held separately.

ZTE translation routes every handled control to ZX-specific positions, covering DMACR with ICR with MIS with RIS with IMSC with IFLS with CR with FBRD with IBRD with shared LCRH plus FR plus DR, with a single line-format position serving both receive and transmit halves.

Vendor profiles differ in translation choice and trigger thresholds and flag positions and boolean capabilities, spanning access_32b with set_uartclk_rate with skip_ibrd_fbrd with fixed_options with always_enabled with cts_event_workaround with dma_threshold with oversampling, each profile paired with its own sizing helper.

Register access combines mapped base in membase with translation-table result from reg_offset and selects wide versus narrow relaxed operations from iotype, centralising every read and write through offset lookup.

Programmed reception scans while the empty flag is clear within a bounded call, counting every accepted byte, routing raw error indications to overrun with frame with parity with break tallies, deriving delivery markers FRAME with PARITY with BREAK with NORMAL from the masked value, with system-request filtering preceding insertion.

System-request preparation is either inert and always declines, or armed to accept a non-zero byte only inside a pending window in sysrq, recording the byte in sysrq_ch and disarming on success through mask or toggle paths, otherwise disarming and declining.

Break handling invokes an optional port callback in handle_break, then manages a timed window in sysrq for console ports flagged by has_sysrq with magic-request support, toggling between arming and disarming, and finally applies secure-attention handling when flagged.
Transmit and receive DMA staging extent is defined as PAGE_SIZE, shared by allocation and release paths.

DMA discovery treats transmit as required and receive as optional, accepting named channels rx with tx lookup with platform-filter fallback and deferral propagation, anchoring slave endpoints at the data register with single-byte width and direction-specific bursts scaled from fifo depth, abandoning receive when residue granularity is descriptor-only, and sourcing poll controls from platform values or device-tree flags poll-timeout-ms with poll-rate-ms with auto-poll plus interval and timeout fallbacks.
Buffer lifecycle pairs coherent allocation with matching release, while channel lifecycle pairs successful acquisition with release on removal for dmarx with dmatx, tolerating absent receive channel.

Transmit DMA sizing withholds a trailing byte for flow restart and stays within page staging and controller alignment, while eligibility excludes small occupancies below half depth; mapping or preparation failures report busy without queueing, and success submits and enables, advances the transmit account, and may request upper-layer wakeup on low occupancy.

Transmit completion runs under the port lock with interrupt state preserved, refreshing the cached DMA control image without transmit enable, releasing any prior mapping marked queued, and either clearing the queued marker for terminal states or attempting refill with programmed I/O fallback.
Transmit accounting advances xmit_fifo past the dispatched extent and adds the same extent to the tx tally.

Stopped or drained transmitters halt; otherwise a pending special character in x_char takes precedence; DMA is preferred when active; remaining queue contents drain through bounded programmed writes in interrupt context, issuing wakeup on low occupancy and stopping when emptied.
Single-character programmed write refuses when called outside interrupt context with the transmit-full flag set, otherwise places the byte in the data register and counts it.

DMA transmit interrupt helper is either inert and always declines, or active to reconcile queued state with enable image and interrupt masking, attempting to queue work and suppressing the transmit interrupt on success.

Transmit-stop operation masks the transmit interrupt and halts DMA transmission, diverting through RS485 sequencing when that mode is enabled and a transfer state is active, including early diversion while in WAIT_AFTER_RTS.
DMA transmit halt is either a no-op without engine support, or clears the transmit enable in the cached image and device when a buffer is marked queued.

Awaiting post-RTS delay cancels trigger_start_tx; active transmission enters post-send wait; drain completion versus configured delay selects distinct waits via trigger_stop_tx; all terminal paths converge on immediate shutdown.
Immediate RS485 shutdown programs request-to-send polarity from after-send policy, re-enabling the receiver while disabling the transmitter, and returns the sequencer to idle.
Transmitter-empty query samples the flag register with vendor errata inversion applied, reporting empty only when neither busy nor transmit-full indications are present.
Stopped definition is true when the line discipline signals flow stop or hardware stop is latched.

With a special character pending the starter temporarily suppresses DMA, requesting interrupt cover when the fifo is full and otherwise emitting directly and restoring prior enable state; without such pending it ensures queuing and enablement; without engine use it reports unsupported.

Transmit flush annotation releases and reacquires the port lock around termination of any in-flight channel and release of a queued mapping with enable image cleared, acting only when DMA transmission is in use.
Vendor fifo depths are 64 [CITED] for ST and 32 [CITED] for Nvidia and 16 [CITED] for ZTE.
Receive DMA polling fallbacks are 100 [CITED] milliseconds for rate and 3000 [CITED] milliseconds for timeout, applied when platform or device-tree values are absent.
Programmed receive drain is capped at 256 [CITED] bytes per call, and the port type name store holds 12 [CITED] characters.

Transmit mapping or preparation failures must not leave a queued marker set, otherwise completion would release an invalid mapping; receive DMA must be refused when residue granularity cannot report progress, otherwise poll accounting would stall; alignment shrinkage must leave its remainder for programmed output, otherwise tail bytes would be lost; withholding a trailing byte preserves a restart trigger for flow control.

A transmit interrupt arriving while a DMA buffer is queued signals a special character rather than completion, requiring the enable image to be reasserted and the interrupt masked; completion must inspect the cached enable image before deciding between refill and termination, otherwise a concurrent stop could strand queued state.

RS485 shutdown must wait for drain and configured delays via timers before deasserting request-to-send, otherwise line turnaround would truncate; programmed reception must respect the empty flag and bounded scan, and programmed transmission must respect the full flag outside interrupt context, otherwise overruns or starvation could follow.
